From 30fe3f5f6494f827d812ff179f295a8e532709d6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pengpeng Hou <pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 22:20:33 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] NFC: pn533: bound the UART receive buffer

pn532_receive_buf() appends every incoming byte to dev->recv_skb and
only resets the buffer after pn532_uart_rx_is_frame() recognizes a
complete frame. A continuous stream of bytes without a valid PN532 frame
header therefore keeps growing the skb until skb_put_u8() hits the tail
limit.

Drop the accumulated partial frame once the fixed receive buffer is full
so malformed UART traffic cannot grow the skb past
PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN.

Fixes: c656aa4c27b1 ("nfc: pn533: add UART phy driver")
Signed-off-by: Pengpeng Hou <pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326142033.82297-1-pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c b/drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c
index 6d2f520a5bc8..1b82b7b2a5fa 100644
--- a/drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c
+++ b/drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c
@@ -211,6 +211,9 @@ static size_t pn532_receive_buf(struct serdev_device *serdev,
 
 	timer_delete(&dev->cmd_timeout);
 	for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+		if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb)))
+			skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);
+
 		skb_put_u8(dev->recv_skb, *data++);
 		if (!pn532_uart_rx_is_frame(dev->recv_skb))
 			continue;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a buffer overflow vulnerability in the PN533 UART driver by bounding the receive buffer.

**Modifications in `drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c`:**
- Added a check inside the loop in `pn532_receive_buf()`: if `skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb)` is zero (i.e., the buffer is full), the existing partial frame is discarded by calling `skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0)` before appending the next byte. This prevents the skb from growing beyond `PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN` when malformed traffic continually sends bytes that do not form a valid PN532 frame header.

**Relationships:**
- The change is confined to a single file (`uart.c`) and directly addresses the root cause: the loop previously always appended bytes to `dev->recv_skb` without checking tailroom. The fix introduces a conditional reset of the buffer when it becomes full, ensuring that only valid partial frames accumulate. This maintains the existing behavior for valid frames while preventing indefinite memory consumption under malicious or erroneous input.

Here is the commit message:
NFC: pn533: bound the UART receive buffer

pn532_receive_buf() appends every incoming byte to dev->recv_skb and
only resets the buffer after pn532_uart_rx_is_frame() recognizes a
complete frame. A continuous stream of bytes without a valid PN532 frame
header therefore keeps growing the skb until skb_put_u8() hits the tail
limit.

Drop the accumulated partial frame once the fixed receive buffer is full
so malformed UART traffic cannot grow the skb past
PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN.

Fixes: c656aa4c27b1 ("nfc: pn533: add UART phy driver")
Signed-off-by: Pengpeng Hou <pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326142033.82297-1-pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The `pn532_receive_buf()` function appends every incoming byte to `dev->recv_skb` without checking the available tailroom. It only resets the buffer when `pn532_uart_rx_is_frame()` identifies a complete frame. A continuous stream of malformed bytes that never form a valid PN532 frame header causes the skb to grow unbounded until `skb_put_u8()` hits the tail limit, potentially leading to memory exhaustion or overflow.

Here is the patch:
 
 static size_t pn532_receive_buf(struct serdev_device *serdev,
 				const u8 *data, size_t count)
 {
 	struct pn532_uart_phy *dev = serdev_device_get_drvdata(serdev);
 	size_t i;
 
 	timer_delete(&dev->cmd_timeout);
 	for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+		if (unlikely(!skb_tailroom(dev->recv_skb)))
+			skb_trim(dev->recv_skb, 0);
+
 		skb_put_u8(dev->recv_skb, *data++);
 		if (!pn532_uart_rx_is_frame(dev->recv_skb))
 			continue;
 
 		pn533_recv_frame(dev->priv, dev->recv_skb, 0);
 		dev->recv_skb = alloc_skb(PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN, GFP_KERNEL);
 		if (!dev->recv_skb)
 			return 0;
 	}
 
 	return i;
 }
